hz_saltgrave_coins.description: Take barrow coins from the dead that walk out of the Saltgrave's west and east barrows.
hz_saltgrave_coins.accept_text:
My name's Maud, and I comb this sand for a living. The living's been thin since the barrows opened.

The dead out here were buried with their gold, and now they walk about with it in their pockets. They're old coins with a king on them that nobody remembers. I've got a buyer in the highlands who'll pay for every one, and I'm too old to argue with a wight about it.

They come up out of the west barrow and the east one. Bring me their coins and I'll make it worth your while. Mind your feet on the way over, because the shallows shift.
hz_saltgrave_coins.turn_in_text:
Look at that king. Nobody's spent one of these in a thousand years, and now I'm going to.

You've earned your cut, and then some. Come back if you want more work, because I've got plenty.

hz_saltgrave_lanterns.description: Put out the Barrow Lanterns and lay the Brine-Wights to rest on the Saltgrave's west and east barrows.
hz_saltgrave_lanterns.accept_text:
You've seen the lights out on the barrows at night. My mother called them corpse-lights. They aren't really lights at all. They're the dead who couldn't find their bodies, and they lead the living out into the water.

I lost a boat to them last winter, and I'd like to stop losing things. Go out to the barrows, west and east, and put out the lanterns. The Brine-Wights keep them lit, so put them down as well.

Whatever you do, don't follow a light anywhere it wants you to go.
hz_saltgrave_lanterns.turn_in_text:
It's darker out there tonight, and it's the good kind of dark. It's the kind you can sleep through.

Thank you. I haven't been able to say that to anybody in a long time.

hz_saltgrave_king.description: Cut through the Drowned Barrow-Thanes on the northern barrow and destroy the Brine King.
hz_saltgrave_king.accept_text:
There's a fourth barrow, out on its own to the north, and it belongs to the King. The others are his thanes, and they don't rest because he doesn't.

He walks the top of his barrow at low tide with his crown on, and he doesn't like visitors. I won't lie to you. I wouldn't go alone, and honestly I wouldn't go at all. But if anyone's going to put him back in the ground, it'll be somebody who brought friends.

His Drowned Barrow-Thanes stand round him. Go north past the middle bar, cut your way through them, and put the Brine King down for good.
hz_saltgrave_king.turn_in_text:
You did it. The water's gone still out there for the first time since I came.

That's the best thing I own, and I want you to have it. Don't argue with me about it.

hz_glass_shards.description: Take fused glass shards from the basilisks in the shard fields west of the Glasswaste's mouth.
hz_glass_shards.accept_text:
The basilisks here grow glass on their backs. They lie in the hot sand and it fuses to them a little more every year, until they're walking about wearing a fortune.

I make blades from it. It takes the best edge you'll ever see, and it never rusts. But I've got one good leg left, and I'm keeping it.

The shard fields are west of the canyon mouth, where the sand shines. The basilisks will see you coming, so let them come to you. Bring me the shards off their backs.
hz_glass_shards.turn_in_text:
Feel the edge on that one, but carefully. You see what I mean?

I'll have one of these sharpened for you by the time you're back from wherever you're going next.

hz_glass_kilns.description: Destroy the Kiln-Walkers on the rise north of Durek's camp.
hz_glass_kilns.accept_text:
Whatever burned this canyon never stopped. It's still up on the rise to the north, walking about on its own, and every time one of them comes down, the sand turns to glass under it and my camp gets smaller.

I call them Kiln-Walkers. Water won't help you, but hitting them will. Go up the rise and break as many as you can, and I'll get a season's peace out of it.
hz_glass_kilns.turn_in_text:
I heard them stop. You don't notice a noise like that until it's gone.

This is for your trouble. It isn't much, but it's honest work.

hz_glass_blister.description: Fight through the Glassback Basilisks in the north hollow and kill Old Blister.
hz_glass_blister.accept_text:
There's one basilisk up in the hollow at the north end that's more glass than beast. We call her Old Blister, and she's the reason I've only got one good leg.

She's been growing that hide since before I was born, and nothing I own will cut it. Don't go alone. Take people you trust, go up through the Glassback Basilisks round her, and when she opens her mouth, make sure you aren't standing in front of it.
hz_glass_blister.turn_in_text:
You've got no idea what that means to me. You really don't.

I made this from the first shard I ever took off her, years ago. It's yours now.

hz_tangle_shallows.description: Kill the Mangrove Snappers round the landing and the Shoal Stalkers in the tangles east and west.
hz_tangle_shallows.accept_text:
My name's Koji'ra. My grandmother told me about these shoals when I was small, and everybody laughed at her. I came anyway, and now I'm the one nobody would believe.

The snappers own the water and the stalkers own the trees, and between the two of them I can't get off this beach. The Mangrove Snappers are in the water round the landing, and the Shoal Stalkers hide in the tangles east and west of it.

Thin them out for me. Watch the branches over your head while you do it.
hz_tangle_shallows.turn_in_text:
I walked out to the big island this morning and nothing tried to eat me. That's the first time since I got here.

Thank you. My grandmother would have liked you.

hz_tangle_sap.description: Gather glowing sap from the Rootbound Guardians on the big island.
hz_tangle_sap.accept_text:
The trees out here bleed light. The guardians on the big island carry it inside them, and my grandmother said it came up from the roots of one tree that's older than the isles.

I want to know whether she was right. Go out to the big island and bring me the sap from the guardians. They're slow, but they don't forget a face, so don't hang about.
hz_tangle_sap.turn_in_text:
Look at it move. It isn't sap at all. It's coming up from something a long way down.

She was right all along. I knew she was right.

hz_tangle_grandfather.description: Cut through the Rootbound Guardians on the big island and bring down Grandfather Mangrove.
hz_tangle_grandfather.accept_text:
There's one guardian on the big island that's bigger than all the rest. My grandmother called him Grandfather Mangrove, and she said he walks round the old tree the way a dog walks round a door it's guarding.

I'd like to see that door. I'm not getting past him, and you won't either, not on your own. Bring friends, cut through the Rootbound Guardians, and put him down.
hz_tangle_grandfather.turn_in_text:
He's down at last. Now let's see what he was standing in front of all this time.

Take this with you. You've earned it twice over.

hz_idols_teeth.description: Kill the Lagoon Crocolisks and Jade Serpents in the water round Fizzle's landing.
hz_idols_teeth.accept_text:
Fizzle Brassgut, treasure hunter, at your service! I've got a boat, a map and a lagoon full of drowned gods made of solid jade. What I can't do is get off this beach, because every single thing in the water wants to eat me.

The Lagoon Crocolisks and the Jade Serpents are all round the landing. You'll hear the crocs before you see them. Clear them out and I'll cut you in on the treasure. I mean it, partner.
hz_idols_teeth.turn_in_text:
Look at that! I can see the water! I can see the TREASURE in the water!

This is the best day of my life, and it's only going to get better if you stick around.

hz_idols_jade.description: Take jade idol shards from the drowned trolls on the western and eastern isles.
hz_idols_jade.accept_text:
The trolls who drowned with the idols carry little bits of them. They chipped them off for luck, I reckon, and that didn't work out for them, did it?

The drowned ones on the western and eastern isles still have them. The hexers will try to put a curse on you, so don't let them get their hands up. Bring me enough shards and I can buy a bigger boat.
hz_idols_jade.turn_in_text:
These are going to make me so rich. I mean us. These are going to make us rich.

Here's your share up front, because I'm a goblin of my word.

hz_idols_zunjal.description: Cut through the Drowned Hexers on the northern isle and kill Idol-Keeper Zun'jal.
hz_idols_zunjal.accept_text:
I've got bad news. The biggest idol, on the last isle up north, has a keeper. His name's Zun'jal. He drowned with the rest of them and he didn't let it slow him down one bit.

He's got his Drowned Hexers round him, and he isn't sharing. I'm not asking you to go alone. I'm asking you to bring every friend you've got, go north past the jade isles, and get that keeper out of the way.
hz_idols_zunjal.turn_in_text:
Is he really gone? Then you're looking at Fizzle Brassgut, the richest goblin in the jungle!

Pick whatever you like, partner. You earned it more than I did.

hz_caravan_dunes.description: Kill the Sandscour Scorpids in the dunes and the Caravan Ghouls in the wagon graves to the west.
hz_caravan_dunes.accept_text:
Rizzo Dustwhistle's the name. My family's been looking for this caravan for four generations, and I'm the one who finally found it. Of course it was me.

The trouble is that it's full of scorpids, and of the people who were on it, who aren't really people any more. The Sandscour Scorpids are in the dunes by the landing, and the Caravan Ghouls are in the wagon graves to the west.

Clear me a way in. Watch the sand while you're at it, because it moves.
hz_caravan_dunes.turn_in_text:
I can see a wagon wheel sticking up out of the sand! It could be Grandma's wagon wheel, for all I know.

You've done more in a day than my family did in a century. Thank you.

hz_caravan_manifest.description: Take the manifest pages from the revenants in the drowned market north of the dunes.
hz_caravan_manifest.accept_text:
The caravan's ledger got torn up when they went under. Every guard on that caravan carried a piece of it, because the Master didn't trust anybody.

The revenants in the drowned market, north of the dunes, still have the pages, and they won't give them up without a fight. Bring them back to me, and I'll finally know what's buried here, and where.
hz_caravan_manifest.turn_in_text:
Silk, spice, and a dragon's egg? A DRAGON'S EGG? Oh, Grandma, you weren't making it up.

I owe you more than I can pay right now, but I'll start with this.

hz_caravan_master.description: Get past the Sandstone Colossi at the buried gate and kill the Last Caravan Master.
hz_caravan_master.accept_text:
The ledger says the Master kept the good stuff in his own wagon at the very back. He's still in it, too. He still thinks he's delivering it.

The Sandstone Colossi at the buried gate keep people away from him, and he'll be harder than all of them put together. Bring a crew, go north through the gate to the back of the caravan, and put him to rest. Then I'll finally know what four generations of my family died looking for.
hz_caravan_master.turn_in_text:
It's real, all of it. Four generations of looking, and it's real.

Pick something you like. Pick two if you want, and I won't tell anyone.

hz_kraal_hyenas.description: Kill the Pit Hyenas on the sinkhole floor and the Sinkhole Quillboar in the thornwalls to the west.
hz_kraal_hyenas.accept_text:
My name's Brannoc. The ground opened up under the Barrens and I came down on a rope to see why. The rope's gone now, and so is the way I came in.

The Pit Hyenas fell in the same way I did, and the Sinkhole Quillboar were already down here waiting. The hyenas roam the sinkhole floor, and the quillboar keep to the thornwalls west of it. Clear them out for me so I can think.
hz_kraal_hyenas.turn_in_text:
The floor's quiet now. I can hear drums further in, though, and I don't think that's better.

Thank you all the same. You've bought me some peace to work out what's going on.

hz_kraal_bones.description: Take the carved prayer-bones from the thornspeakers in the thornwalls and at the shrine-pool to the north.
hz_kraal_bones.accept_text:
The thornspeakers down here carry bones carved with prayers. I want to know who they're praying to in a hole like this, because something's answering them.

They keep to the thornwalls in the west and the shrine-pool to the north. They'll pray at you when you get close, and it's best to ignore it. Bring me the bones and I'll read them.
hz_kraal_bones.turn_in_text:
Every one of these says the same name over and over. It's the Thorn-Mother.

She isn't alive, and from what I can read, she doesn't need to be.

hz_kraal_mother.description: Fight through the Kraal Bonewalkers at the north end and destroy the Thorn-Mother's Echo.
hz_kraal_mother.accept_text:
Her seat is at the north end, above everything else down here. Her dead walk round it, and she walks among them, or what's left of her does.

She's the reason the ground opened. I'm sure of it now. Bring friends, go north to her seat, and get through the Kraal Bonewalkers that guard it. She'll sing, and the thorns will listen to her. If you put her down, maybe the ground closes again.
hz_kraal_mother.turn_in_text:
The drums have stopped. Thank you for that.

I think I can find a way back up now. If I make it, I'll tell the Barrens who to thank.

hz_glade_wisps.description: Put out the Gloomwisps along the shadowed path near the glade's entrance.
hz_glade_wisps.accept_text:
My name's Ithrael. My grandmother put the seal on this glade and she never spoke about it. I've come to read what she wouldn't say.

The Gloomwisps lead people off the path and leave them there to wander. They keep to the shadowed path near where you came in. Put them out before they do the same to me.
hz_glade_wisps.turn_in_text:
It's darker now, but it's an honest dark, and I'll take it.

Thank you. I can start reading now without wondering what's behind me.

hz_glade_sentinels.description: Free the Shades of the Sentinel in the silent grove to the west and kill the Moonless Satyrs in the twisted hollow to the east.
hz_glade_sentinels.accept_text:
The Sentinels my grandmother left here are still on watch. They died on watch, and they don't know they're allowed to stop.

The satyrs came because the Sentinels can't see them any more. The Shades of the Sentinel stand in the silent grove to the west, and the Moonless Satyrs have taken the twisted hollow to the east. Free the Sentinels, and put an end to the satyrs.
hz_glade_sentinels.turn_in_text:
They went quietly. I think they were glad to go. The satyrs weren't glad about anything.

My grandmother would want me to thank you, so I am.

hz_glade_priestess.description: Go to the sealed shrine at the north end of the glade and destroy the Unlit Priestess and the shades that guard her.
hz_glade_priestess.accept_text:
I've read it all now. A priestess here prayed to Elune for something she shouldn't have, Elune turned away, and the moon hasn't shone on this glade since.

She's still in the sealed shrine at the north end, still praying, and the Shades of the Sentinel still guard her door. She won't stop praying long enough to talk. Go with friends, and give her an answer.
hz_glade_priestess.turn_in_text:
The clouds are thinning. Look up there, can you see it?

Thank you. Take whatever you like from what I've got. Tonight, I don't need any of it.

hz_storm_rams.description: Kill the Thunderhide Rams on the crag path and the Stormcrag Harpies nesting in the east ring.
hz_storm_rams.accept_text:
Halvard Grey, and I chase storms. This one never moves, which makes it either the easiest storm in the world to study or the most dangerous.

The Thunderhide Rams charge anything that moves on the crag path, and the Stormcrag Harpies nest in the east ring. I need both of them out of the way so I can set up my rods.
hz_storm_rams.turn_in_text:
My rods are up. Now we wait for the lightning, and I don't think we'll be waiting long.

Thank you. This storm's been here a hundred years, and we're finally going to learn why.

hz_storm_shards.description: Take storm shards from the stormlings up on the thunder table to the north.
hz_storm_shards.accept_text:
The stormlings up here carry shards with lightning still inside them. If I can read enough of them, I can tell you what's calling the storm.

They're thickest on the thunder table to the north. They'll shock you, and that's how you'll know it's working. Bring me their shards.
hz_storm_shards.turn_in_text:
It's the stone, the big one at the very top. The storm isn't sitting here by accident. Something is calling it.

I've got one more thing to ask of you, and it's the dangerous one.

hz_storm_stone.description: Get past the Stone-Circle Wardens at the top of the crag and break the Calling Stone.
hz_storm_stone.accept_text:
The stone at the top calls the storm, and the wardens in the rings keep anyone from getting near it. Somebody made them for that. Somebody wanted this storm here.

Go north to the very top of the crag, get through the Stone-Circle Wardens and break the stone. Bring friends who don't mind being struck by lightning. Don't wear anything metal. I'm joking, mostly.
hz_storm_stone.turn_in_text:
Look at that. It's blue sky, for the first time in a hundred years, if the old books are right.

You earned this. Take it, and tell people what you saw up here.

hz_orchard_rows.description: Put down the Orchard Scarecrows and Orchard Ghouls in the grey rows west of the gate.
hz_orchard_rows.accept_text:
My name's Marta. My family grew apples here before the plague. I died in that house over there, and when I woke up I walked straight back to it. It's funny how that works.

The Orchard Scarecrows don't know me any more, and the Orchard Ghouls never did. They're in the grey rows west of the gate. The scarecrows only look like they're standing still, so be careful.
hz_orchard_rows.turn_in_text:
Thank you. I walked the rows just now for the first time in years.

My father planted those trees. I'd forgotten how straight he made the lines.

hz_orchard_cider.description: Stop the Plague Pickers in the cider house to the east and the Rotfruit Bats carrying off the fruit.
hz_orchard_cider.accept_text:
The pickers in the cider house are still pressing apples, and the apples are plagued. Somebody's going to drink that one day.

Go east to the cider house and stop the Plague Pickers. The Rotfruit Bats eat the fallen fruit and carry it off, so they need stopping too. They're everywhere, so look up.
hz_orchard_cider.turn_in_text:
No more cider. I never thought I'd be glad to say that.

You've stopped the plague spreading out of this orchard, and I won't forget it.

hz_orchard_bramley.description: Put down the Orchard Scarecrows under the old tree to the north, and destroy Old Bramley.
hz_orchard_bramley.accept_text:
My father made the first scarecrow in this orchard and named it Bramley after the apple. It stands under the old tree to the north now with a scythe, and the plague's in it, and it won't stop.

Please put it down. Take friends, because it was built to keep things away, and it's good at it. The Orchard Scarecrows round it will come at you first.
hz_orchard_bramley.turn_in_text:
He's finally down. Father would have hated what it turned into.

Thank you. Take something from the house, because I've got no use for any of it now.

hz_root_listen.description: Quiet the Lost Rootspeakers along the roots and kill the Heartwood Spiders in the galleries.
hz_root_listen.accept_text:
My name's Ash'ka, and I'm Koji'ra's grandmother. I told her about this tree when she was small, and then I came to find it myself, and it kept me. I don't mind. It's beautiful down here.

The Darkspear who followed me down stopped listening to the roots and started speaking for them, and they're wrong about what the tree wants. Go through the amber hollows and out along the roots, quiet the Lost Rootspeakers, and clear the Heartwood Spiders out of the dark galleries between.
hz_root_listen.turn_in_text:
Listen to that. Can you hear it? It's the tree, not them.

It's been a long time since I could hear it that clearly. Thank you.

hz_root_amber.description: Go into the heartwood and destroy Amberheart, the Sap-Mother.
hz_root_amber.accept_text:
In the heartwood, there's a pool of sap that woke up. We call her Amberheart. She was meant to feed the tree, and she's started keeping it all for herself, and the tree's getting hungry.

You'll find the heartwood in the middle of everything, and you'll know it by the light. She'll seal you in amber if she can, so bring friends who can cut you out.
hz_root_amber.turn_in_text:
The sap's running again. Can you feel it? It's warm all the way down.

The tree's going to remember this. So am I.

hz_root_father.description: Put the Root-Father back to sleep, and kill Gnarl the Unburied in the knotted dark to the west.
hz_root_father.accept_text:
At the very bottom of the tree, which is the top of everything down here, the oldest root of all has woken up. We call him the Root-Father. He was here before the isles were, and he's angry that anyone found him.

Old Gnarl the Unburied, out in the knotted dark to the west, has been feeding him. Go up through the knotted deep to the Root-Father's bed and put them both back to sleep. Don't go alone. Nobody should go anywhere alone down here.
hz_root_father.turn_in_text:
He's sleeping, and the whole tree just sighed. Did you hear it?

Take this, and then go and tell my granddaughter that I'm happy here. She'll want to know.

hz_vault_quiet.description: Give rest to the Palimpsest Wraiths and the Erasures in the vault's outer stacks.
hz_vault_quiet.accept_text:
I was the librarian here, before the Bloom and before the Scourge, and before most things you'd know about. I stayed because somebody has to know where everything is.

The Palimpsest Wraiths are what's left of the books the Bloom wrote over, and the Erasures are what's left of the people who read them. They're in the outer stacks. Go round, because everything down here goes round, and give them rest.
hz_vault_quiet.turn_in_text:
It's quieter now. You can almost hear the pages turning, and that's a good sound, down here.

Thank you. I'd forgotten what the vault sounded like.

hz_vault_pages.description: Take the scraped pages from the drowned scholars on the vault's inner shelves.
hz_vault_pages.accept_text:
The scholars who drowned in the ink carry pages that have been scraped clean. But a scraped page remembers, if you know how to read it.

They walk the inner shelves. You'll have to find the way in, because the gate into each ring is on a different side. Bring me their pages and I'll read what was written on them first.
hz_vault_pages.turn_in_text:
Here it is, under the Bloom's writing and under the one before that. It's a name, and it's the Keeper's.

He's still here, at the top of the vault, still trying to finish the first page.

hz_vault_keeper.description: Destroy the Last Editor at the heart of the rings and the Keeper of the First Page beyond the top of the vault.
hz_vault_keeper.accept_text:
The Keeper has been trying to finish the first page for longer than there have been people to read it. The Last Editor, at the heart of the vault, strikes out every word he writes. They'll never finish, and while they try, nothing down here can rest.

The Editor sits at the heart of the rings, and the Keeper reads alone beyond the top of the vault. End it for both of them, and take everyone you trust.
hz_vault_keeper.turn_in_text:
It's finished at last. I don't mean the page. I mean the trying.

Take one of these. I've been keeping them for whoever finally managed it.

hz_pines_webs.description: Kill the Gloom Spiders in the pine wood west of the track.
hz_pines_webs.accept_text:
My name's Ilsabet. I came here to study the mere, and I've stayed because I can't bear to leave it unfinished.

The Gloom Spiders in the west wood hang their kills in the pines, and then the kills come down again on their own. I'd like fewer of both. They're west of the track where the pines are thickest, so look up before you look down.
hz_pines_webs.turn_in_text:
It's quieter out there. I can hear the water again, which isn't better, but at least I know where it is.

Thank you. That's one less thing watching me from the trees.

hz_pines_water.description: Gather vials of mere-water from the wraiths at the mere and the shrine north of it.
hz_pines_water.accept_text:
The wraiths at the mere are made of the water itself. If you break one apart, there's a little left that won't drain away, and that's what I need. It remembers things, and I want to know what.

They keep to the mere and the shrine north of it. Bring me the water, and don't drink any of it. I know you weren't going to.
hz_pines_water.turn_in_text:
Hold one up to the light. Can you see the shapes? Those are the pines, from before they died.

Thank you, truly. I couldn't have done this without you.

hz_pines_weeping.description: Kill the Weeping Worgen on the track and the Rotbark Treants in the drowned copse east of the mere.
hz_pines_weeping.accept_text:
The worgen here don't hunt. They walk the track and weep, and if you get between one of them and the water it'll tear you apart to get past. The Rotbark Treants in the drowned copse east of the mere have started doing the same.

I've read enough to know they aren't the cause, but they're in the way of it. Clear the Weeping Worgen off the track and the treants out of the copse. They won't stop crying, so try not to let it get to you.
hz_pines_weeping.turn_in_text:
It was never the worgen. It's her, and it always was.

I know what we have to do now, and I don't like it.

hz_pines_widow.description: Wait for the fog at the mere, then destroy the Widow of the Mere and her Mere Wraiths.
hz_pines_widow.accept_text:
She drowned herself in the mere after the pines died, and she took the wood with her. That's what the vials showed me. Everything here weeps because she does.

She rises out of the water when the fog's thickest, with her Mere Wraiths round her. I can't fight her, and you can't either, not alone. Bring people who aren't afraid of crying things, and don't listen when she says your name.
hz_pines_widow.turn_in_text:
The fog's thinning. I can see the far shore for the first time.

I think I can go home now. Take this with you. I won't need it where I'm going.
